summary: Both blocking findings are valid. The spec needs an explicit continuation handoff contract and a recovery candidate selectability matrix before implementation can proceed.

items.title: Selected runId is specified as a guard but not as a continuation resolver
items.rationale: The current spec requires guarded continuation by runId but does not state how next-action and run commands load the selected recovery candidate. That is a real implementation blocker.
items.evidence: spec.json requirements R3-R5 mention selected runId verification, while overview data flow does not specify candidate execution root or a runId resolver.

items.title: Recovery candidate states do not define which runId-bearing candidates are continuable
items.target: Overview Data Flow / R2 / R3 / Acceptance Criteria
items.rationale: The current spec distinguishes finalized and missing-runId candidates, but leaves stale, orphan-worktree, and branch-only runId-bearing candidates ambiguous.
items.evidence: spec.json R2 lists candidate states and R3 says candidates with runId can be selected, while acceptance criteria only explicitly block finalized and missing-runId candidates.
